name: Mitolo Shiraz Savitar 2018
text:
## Mitolo Shiraz Savitar 2018

**The story.** Mitolo is a family-owned McLaren Vale winery founded and led by Frank Mitolo, who set out to draw on his Italian heritage to make wines "of individuality, integrity and utmost quality". In a short time it has come to be recognised as one of the finest producers in McLaren Vale ([Vintus, the US importer](https://bnog.vintus.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Mitolo-Savitar-Shiraz-2018-Tech.pdf)).

**The wine: Savitar.** "Savitar" is a mythical dragon-like monster. Frank Mitolo and Ben Glaetzer, of the Barossa's Glaetzer winemaking family, named the wine for the impression one small lot in their Willunga vineyard made on them: they were "so blown away" that they decided to bottle it on its own ([Vintus](https://bnog.vintus.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Mitolo-Savitar-Shiraz-2018-Tech.pdf)). The fruit comes from the Chinese Block of the Lopresti vineyards in the Willunga district, at the southern end of [McLaren Vale](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Willunga,+South+Australia,+Australia&t=k), from an unforgiving, skeletal patch of soil in the block's north-east corner, where the vines struggle and give very low yields. Each parcel spends 15 days on its skins, a little longer than usual, for a tighter structure built for ageing; then 18 months in new, medium-to-light-toast French oak, after which individual barrels are chosen for the final blend. It is 100% [Shiraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah), at 14.5% alcohol ([Vintus](https://bnog.vintus.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Mitolo-Savitar-Shiraz-2018-Tech.pdf); [Vintus, 2018](https://bnog.vintus.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Mitolo-Savitar-Shiraz-2018-Tech.pdf)).

**From the history books**
- **Named for a McLaren.** McLaren Vale was named after either David McLaren, Colonial Manager of the South Australian Company, or John McLaren, who surveyed the area in 1839. The first settlers grew cereal crops, but John Reynell and Thomas Hardy planted vines in 1838, and the forerunners of today's Seaview and Hardys wineries were running by 1850 ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)).
- **Century-old vines.** Some McLaren Vale vines more than 100 years old are still producing ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)), and the region is a member of the Great Wine Capitals of the World network.
- **Between the gulf and the hills.** The region runs 30 km down the coast of the [Gulf St Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulf_St_Vincent) to the foothills of the [Mount Lofty Ranges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Lofty_Ranges), with a [Mediterranean climate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediterranean_climate) of four clear seasons ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLaren_Vale)).
- **Penfolds comes south.** Between 1904 and 1912 [Penfolds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds), then the largest winery around Adelaide, bought vineyards in McLaren Vale ([Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penfolds)).

**The vintage.** [Jancis Robinson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jancis_Robinson)'s [South Australia vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/south-australia) calls 2018 very promising; the most bullish commentators called it great everywhere, while more circumspect ones noted that early frosts cut yields, with good, consistent weather in the second half of the season.

**What the critics say for 2018.**
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 95** (Joe Czerwinski, February 2021, quoted on [Vintus's tech sheet](https://bnog.vintus.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Mitolo-Savitar-Shiraz-2018-Tech.pdf)). "More high-toned and red-fruited": cherry-scented, with vanilla, cedar and dried spices from the oak and some darker berry notes. Full-bodied, "but tighter and more age-worthy than the GAM or Angela", Mitolo's other Shirazes, "with a taut, lingering finish".
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.0** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eight years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2024 to 2033, and the Advocate singled it out as built to age. So it is just entering its drinking window, with years ahead: open one now with a long decant (two hours), or wait a few years for more mellow, savoury notes. Serve at 16 to 18°C.

**Food.** Slow-cooked beef short ribs, a peppered steak, or lamb shoulder with rosemary.

**Value and where to buy.** None of the stores on this site lists Mitolo at the moment.

Sources:
- [Vintus, Mitolo Savitar Shiraz 2018 tech sheet (PDF)](https://bnog.vintus.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Mitolo-Savitar-Shiraz-2018-Tech.pdf)
- [Jancis Robinson, South Australia vintage chart](https://www.jancisrobinson.com/learn/vintages/south-australia)
